Tim Southee | KKR's bowling coach: "The powerplay hasn't been ideal throughout the IPL, but the guys have been able to come back outside of the powerplay onwards brilliantly. Our spinners are doing a great job through the middle here. (On Kartik Tyagi) He's been brilliant. I think we've been very impressed with him throughout the lead-up, the way he's trained in the games he had before the tournament, and we're seeing his brilliance throughout the tournament. For a young kid, he's had a number of setbacks over the years, a number of injuries, and to see him playing consistently and doing well, bowling quick, but also with control, it's been very impressive. (On Sunil Narine) He's brilliant. He's a great thinker of the game. He's obviously been around for a long time, but the longer you're around, the more people see of you, but Sunny still seems to find a way to go at six and a bit an over every IPL. He's an absolute genius, so to have someone like him in our side along with Varun, who's got an incredible IPL record as well, makes games like this where sides get off to a flier in the powerplay and yet you hit them with those two spinners, it's a handy tool to have."
Strategic timeout! What a phase for KKR. Their spinners absolutely dominated that phase from the 7th to 14th over. Four wickets taken and very few runs conceded. Would be interesting to see how the DC batters finish off the innings. Will they need an impact sub in the form of Porel or Karun Nair? We'll find out soon..
